positive: Many commenters praise the opening and closing animation as smooth, clean and clever, including some who say they usually prefer other brands.
Viewers see the matte inner screen as a smart way to hide the crease, and some say no crease is visible.
Some note the animation reacts to the hinge angle, suggesting developers could build new effects, and it is seen as typical of Apple's attention to detail.
negative: Several viewers see the fold animation as a superficial gimmick, noting that a fan has already recreated it on a rival foldable.
Commenters criticise the high price, especially outside the US, and compare it unfavourably with cheaper rival foldables and worry about repair costs.

positive: Several commenters credit Samsung for pioneering foldables and supplying the screen, while saying they are happy to stay with their Fold.
Some see Apple's entry as good for the market, expecting rivals to respond and the category to grow, with a few now interested in buying a foldable.
negative: Commenters say Samsung and other Android makers released foldable phones many years ago, so Apple's version looks late and unoriginal.
Many mock Apple fans for getting excited about features that Android users have had for years, and say Apple is simply copying Samsung.
Some point out that Apple once dismissed foldables, and that Samsung supplies Apple's screens. A few predict Apple will drop the product soon.

positive: Many commenters were pleasantly surprised by the iPhone Duo's design, praising its minimal crease, matte inner screen, unfolding animation and the aspect ratio when open.
Several Samsung Fold 8 owners and fans said they prefer Samsung's squarer, rectangular, thin and light design, though some welcomed Apple to foldables.
Some Apple fans plan to buy the Duo for its software, ecosystem and durability, and say the missing telephoto lens and Touch ID don't bother them.
negative: Many commenters say Apple is arriving years after Samsung and Google with foldables, yet presents the idea as new and groundbreaking.
Price draws criticism: commenters say the cost matches an iPhone plus an iPad, so expectations are high and value is questioned.

The outer screen shape, aspect ratio and uneven rounded corners are called awkward or impractical, with some disliking the matte display; some say Samsung's front screen and desktop features are better.

positive: Many commenters expected a higher price for Apple's foldable and were pleasantly surprised it launched lower than predicted.
Several note the price is in line with Samsung's foldables and typical for the category, seeing it as competitive or fair.
Some argue the cost is reasonable when compared with early foldables and inflation, or say the larger screen and Apple ecosystem justify it.
negative: Many commenters see the foldable's price as excessive, saying it costs about as much as two regular phones and that a phone this expensive should not be normal.
Commenters in India, Mexico, Australia and Europe say local prices are especially steep compared with local incomes and with rival foldables, putting the phone out of reach for most people.
Some say the high cost is not worth it for them personally, whether because they cannot afford it or do not want a foldable.

positive: Many commenters prefer an uninterrupted inner screen without a cutout or dot, and say they would trade selfie quality on that display for it.
Several say they rarely use the inner display for selfies, since the outer screen camera is better and easier for photos, or they don't care much about cameras.
Some praise the polished camera animation and open/close transitions, and think the feature will push other brands to improve under-display cameras.
negative: Many commenters say under-display cameras aren't new, citing earlier phones, particularly Samsung's, so they don't see this as an Apple innovation.
Several note the camera is still noticeable on the inner screen, so it isn't truly hidden, and some find it looks unappealing.

positive: Some hope for a software option to move the dock or controls to the left, or note the device could be rotated.
negative: Many left-handed commenters say the Duo's interface and layout are built around right-handed one-handed use, making it awkward or frustrating for them.
Several note this goes beyond software: the fingerprint sensor, outer display, cameras and a right-shifted dock are placed for right-handers, so a mirrored design or setting would be needed.
Some ask for a handedness option or say they'll skip the phone, while a few say left-handers can adapt or have other reasons not to buy.

positive: Apple Pencil compatibility on the foldable was a pleasant surprise and a deciding factor for several viewers, who said it pushed them to preorder or switch.
Some Samsung foldable owners see pencil support as an advantage over their own device, and hope stylus support returns to Samsung's folds.
Pencil support is valued alongside other features like water resistance and the larger inner screen, which viewers see as useful for productivity and a mini-tablet style of use.
negative: Many commenters say Apple is copying Samsung and other rivals, and has stopped innovating, so praise from Apple fans seems undeserved.
Several see Apple's lack of full Apple Pencil support as a letdown, noting that missing pressure sensitivity limits drawing on the go.

positive: Many commenters praise the fold and unfold transition animation, calling it smooth, clean and like looking through glass to the inner screen.
The nano-texture inner display is liked for its matte look, reduced fingerprints and for helping hide the fold crease.
Some see the foldable as a compelling mix of iPhone and small tablet, citing durability, pencil support and flexible screen layouts.
negative: Many commenters say the nano-texture (matte) finish lowers clarity, vibrancy and brightness, and some think it is worse in sunlight than a glossy screen.
Some prefer a glossy inner display, accepting a slight crease over a matte finish, and find the glossy-to-matte change between outer and inner screens odd.
Commenters also worry about the inner screen's durability, since it cannot take a screen protector, and doubt the crease reduction is worth the trade-off.

positive: Many commenters say they are excited and ready to preorder, with some counting down to launch and already lining up accessories.
Owners of older iPhones, who had held off upgrading for years, see the Duo as a compelling reason to finally switch.
negative: Many like the idea but find the price too high, especially compared with the Pro Max, and some say regional pricing is worse.
Several plan to wait for a second or later generation, expecting fixes to first-version problems such as weak cameras, screen durability and weight.
Some think it is too heavy or too similar to an iPad mini, so they would stick with a Pro Max or a tablet.

positive: Several commenters like the official folio case, saying it looks good, protects the front screen from smudges and scratches, and even converts them from going caseless.
Many are drawn to the Duo overall, citing smooth fold animations, a barely visible crease, MagSafe and Touch ID, though price gives some pause.
negative: Folio and kickstand cases are seen as clumsy: the cover blocks the camera, slows quick payments, and adds too many flaps.
Many worry about protecting such an expensive foldable, especially the outer screen and edges, since bumper-style cases seem hard to fit.
A case adds to what is already a thick, heavy, bulky device, and some doubt it would stop the wobble.

positive: Many commenters expect a well-known durability YouTuber to put the phone through bend and break tests, and joke or speculate about how it will hold up.
Some think Apple designed the phone, including reinforced antenna lines, with that kind of testing in mind and expect it to survive.
Reactions are mixed on first-generation risk: some are excited to buy and test it themselves, while others prefer to wait or stay with their current model.
negative: Commenters worry the phone is fragile and could break from a single drop, with some pointing to the antenna line as a structural weak point.
Some criticise the high price given that durability appears untested, and note the screen scratches at fairly low levels of the scratch test.

positive: Night Sky, the dark blue-black shade, is the most popular color choice, praised as clean, understated and attractive.
Several commenters are torn between Night Sky and white, with white or silver seen as a classic Apple look.
Higher storage tiers are favored by those who mention capacity, and some plan to pair their phone with a taupe folio case.
negative: Many commenters worry about battery life and drain, and dislike that Apple doesn't disclose battery capacity or show a percentage in the battery icon.
Storage tiers are seen as very expensive in Australia and New Zealand, with local prices well above currency-converted US prices.
Colour options and names draw criticism: people want plain black or white, and some notice colour inaccuracy on the inner display and visible screen creases.

positive: Many like the compact folded size, seeing it as a replacement for small phones like the mini while still offering a large unfolded screen.
Commenters are excited about a genuinely new iPhone design, and some see the foldable as able to replace a tablet.
The software is praised for fitting the folding shape, including smooth open/close animations, screen switching, and a side toolbar that saves vertical space.
negative: Size and pocketability are a worry: some say the device is too bulky or wide to carry or hold comfortably, and would rather get a tablet.
Some dislike design choices, such as a covered or awkward front screen, durability concerns about folding screens, and a high price for the use case.

positive: Animations and transitions when folding and unfolding get particular praise, with some seeing them as a high bar for foldable software design.
Some say the software alone makes them consider switching or buying, while others note rivals offer more functionality and flexibility.
negative: Many commenters mock the idea that Apple is innovating, noting that Samsung and others already made foldables, with Apple mainly adding its own software.
Some see the device as largely Samsung-built hardware with locked-down iOS on top, so Apple's contribution is the software tuning for a folding screen.
Others say software polish may not offset hardware and design drawbacks, and note missing options, such as a feature that can't be toggled.

positive: Many commenters say they plan to buy or pre-order the iPhone Duo, and some Android users express admiration or say they switched.
Viewers praise the software, especially the fold transition animations, and say Apple's performance and optimisation beat rival foldables.
negative: Many commenters mock the name 'Duo' and wish Apple had chosen something else, such as 'Fold', and they compare it to Microsoft's Surface Duo.
Commenters joke that Apple makes minor tweaks, such as a less visible crease, and presents them as innovation. They also say Samsung supplies much of the hardware.
Others criticize the phone as heavy, chunky and awkward to use one-handed, with a very high price, especially for the top storage tier.

positive: Commenters defend the price and build, noting other foldables cost similarly and that durability worries stem from a plastic dummy unit, not the titanium retail phone.
Many are excited by the smooth fold animation and the pocketable tablet-like form, seeing it as useful for travel and for replacing multiple devices.
Several Apple users say they finally want a foldable because it keeps iOS and the ecosystem, and expect competitors and app developers to respond.
negative: Many commenters worry the folding hinge and crease will wear out over time, and that one drop could ruin an exposed device.
Commenters think the roughly $2,000 starting price is unjustified, especially given the economy, and call the base storage too low.
Several say Apple is copying Samsung and others who already sell foldables, so they don't see it as an innovation.

positive: Many praise the design and attention to detail, including the smooth opening animation, the camera bump layout and how well the software suits the hardware.
Several see practical benefits of the wider, book-style form, such as reading documents or patient charts on the move and using it vertically.
Some commenters compare it with foldables from other brands, praising the screen, the ecosystem or other models, while others expect later versions to be better.
negative: Several worry about first-generation risks and durability, including repair costs for the screen, hinge stress from drops, and a crease that is more visible than claimed.
Practical design complaints include a wide body that fits pockets poorly, hinge placement, the matte finish hurting video contrast, rounded corners, and the awkward case when using both cameras.

positive: Many commenters see the foldable as a pocketable stand-in for an iPad or iPad mini, so they could carry one device instead of two.
The larger inner screen is valued for video, gaming, multitasking, reading and viewing plans or manuals, including for people with weaker eyesight.
Design details get praise: the matte screen, the wide passport-like shape for video, sensible button placement and the smooth screen animation.
negative: Many see the foldable as essentially a small iPad in disguise, with little real innovation and arriving years after rival foldables.
Hardware and software drawbacks draw criticism: a matte inner screen that looks poor in sunlight, a crowded home screen, limited dock, and restricted multitasking such as no split apps in landscape.
Concerns about high price, impractical size when folded, difficult cases and repairs, and a wish for reliability fixes over new form factors.

positive: Many commenters praise the redesigned iOS for the foldable, saying it looks polished, is well integrated, and adds real multitasking capability beyond the folding form.
Thoughtful details get credit, such as moving interface elements for the wider display so existing apps fit, and layout choices that suit left-handed users.
Some Android users say they would switch or want iOS on a foldable, preferring its simplicity and feel even over arguably stronger Android foldables.
negative: Many commenters say the price is excessive, especially outside the US, where taxes and conversion push it to several times the US figure.
Several say the multitasking and split-screen features are nothing new, since Android phones and foldables have offered them for years, and that iOS still looks less mature.
Commenters criticise the design and build, citing a visible crease, a clumsy opening mechanism and awkward use for calls, and doubt the presentation is honest.

positive: Commenters praise the hinge as well-engineered, with a durable titanium build that feels more substantial than other foldables or mock-ups.
Some note that water-resistance ratings on foldables usually exclude the hinge, and say brands are not always upfront about this.
The rounded edge and folded look get positive reactions, with people finding it softer, easier to hold and pocket-friendly, and a case that covers the hinge is seen as useful.
negative: Commenters doubt that an IP68 rating means much on a foldable, since the hinge area stays open to dust and sand.
Several say dust ingress has already been seen in other IP68 foldables, so they expect the same here despite the rating.
Some worry about long-term hinge durability from repeated folding, and say they would not take a pricey foldable to the beach without protection.

positive: Many commenters are excited about the foldable and plan to buy early, either at launch or within the next year.
Viewers praise the barely visible crease, the refined design and the Apple ecosystem, saying it improves on other foldables.
negative: Many commenters say Apple is years behind rivals that already sell foldables, so the device feels derivative rather than innovative.
Commenters suspect Apple is deliberately leaving out features, such as the flagship camera, to sell them in next year's model. Some are already waiting for the next version.
The high price and costly extras like insurance are criticised, and many doubt a foldable is useful when a tablet or laptop is at hand.

positive: Many viewers like the Duo and would buy it, but wish it had the camera system from the Pro models.
Some Pro owners would keep their current phone or pair it with a Duo, or wait for a later generation.
negative: Pricing is a major complaint, with high local prices in several countries seen as unjustified and likely to hurt sales.
Other missing features, such as Face ID, a better battery, speakers and a quick action button, add to the reluctance, so some will wait for a later or Pro version.
